name: Juxtlahuaca Mixtec
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Josserand, Judy Kathryn 1983, Mixtec Dialect History (PhD thesis, Tulane) — comparative phonology incl. Juxtlahuaca data; cited on Glottolog page
earlier_scan.note: Josserand 1983 thesis is the named lead; DiCanio/Auderset 2023 Mixtec comparative work another lead

sources.citation: Eischens, Ben & Ryan T. Bennett. 2025. The Mixtec couplet is not a consistent grammatical unit. Glossa (lingbuzz/009245 preprint).
sources.note: Cites San Martín Duraznos Mixtec (Auderset et al. 2024) only for enclitic nasality patterns (p.~12); its stress discussion concerns San Martín Peras (west2643), not vmc.

sources.citation: DiCanio, Christian & Ryan Bennett. 2018 [2020]. Prosody in Mesoamerican languages. Preprint of chapter in The Oxford Handbook of Language Prosody.
sources.note: Family-level survey only (§2.2, pp.4–5): stress in Oto-Manguean is fixed and confined to roots; for 14 Mixtecan languages 7 root-initial, 4 root-final, 3 variable; no Juxtlahuaca/Duraznos variety is named.

sources.citation: Caballero, Gabriela, Claudia Duarte Borquez, Claudia Juárez Chávez & Michelle Yuan. 2026. Lexical and grammatical tone in San Juan Piñas Mixtec (Tò'ōn Ndá'ví). Phonological Data and Analysis 8, e7: 1–36. doi:10.1017/S2642182825000029
sources.note: No word-stress statement. §2 p.5: the bimoraic couplet 'is equivalent to a metrical foot, aligned at the right edge of a prosodic word' (following Carroll 2015, Penner 2019, Uchihara & Mendoza Ruiz 2022); 'stress' appears only for Spanish loan source words (fn) and 'accentuation' only as a process reported for other Mixtec varieties (fn 16).

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra, Carmen Hernández Martínez & Albert Ventayol-Boada. 2024. Constituency in Tù'un Ntá'ví (Mixtec) of San Martín Duraznos. In A. J. R. Tallman, S. Auderset & H. Uchihara (eds.), Constituency and convergence in the Americas, 265–304. Berlin: Language Science Press. doi:10.5281/zenodo.13208550
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM121.C66 2024); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PM121 .C66 2024
sources.note: Silent on stress. §2.1 (p.267) gives the phonological background: three tonemes H/L/M, every vowel tone-marked, no final consonants, long vowels = two vowels; §3.1 'Bimoraicity constraint' (p.277) states lexical free forms are minimally bimoraic (CVCV, CVV, CVʔV, VCV) as in other Mixtec 'prosodic words'. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 40 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent the text).

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2024. Procesos morfofonológicos de pronombres y clasificadores en el Tù'un Ntá'ví (mixteco) de San Martín Duraznos. Talk handout, IIFL-UNAM, 2 Feb 2024 (27 slides).
sources.note: Silent on stress. Slide 8 'Unas características del idioma': words generally bimoraic (monosyllabic or disyllabic), grammatical words may be monomoraic, 3 tonemes (alto/medio/bajo), little tone sandhi.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra. 2024. Rates of change and phylogenetic signal in Mixtec tone. Language Dynamics and Change. doi:10.1163/22105832-bja10031
sources.note: Comparative tone-change study; no statement about stress in any variety (only a bibliography hit on McKendry 2013 'prominence').

sources.citation: Van Doren, Maxine, Claudia Duarte Borquez, Claudia Juárez Chávez & Gabriela Caballero. 2024 [2025]. San Juan Piñas Mixtec (Illustration of the IPA). JIPA 54(2): 853–882. doi:10.1017/S002510032400015X — authors give ISO 639-3 vmc; Glottolog files San Juan Piñas (sanj1280) under west2643.
sources.note: Silent on word stress: no occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the text; prosodic statements are about the bimoraic 'couplet' (root) as the domain of glottalization, nasal-vowel distribution and preaspiration.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra & Adam J. R. Tallman. 2023. Wordhood and alignment in Duraznos Mixtec pronouns. Talk handout, Universität Bern, 2 Dec 2023 (31 slides).
sources.note: Silent on stress. Background slide: lexical elements minimally bimoraic, grammatical elements can be monomoraic; 3 tonemes; TBU is the mora, each mora specified for tone; word order VSO.

sources.citation: Ventayol-Boada, Albert. 2021. From classifiers to subordination: Nominal origins of relativizers and subordinators in Tù'un na ñuu Sá Mátxíí Ntxè'è (Mixtec). Amerindia 43.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Only other published SMD-specific paper; syntax-focused but may carry a phonological background section. Journal site (sedyl.cnrs.fr/amerindia) returned only stubs/cert errors by automated download.

sources.citation: Padgett, Erin. 2017. Tools for assessing relatedness in understudied language varieties: A survey of Mixtec varieties in western Oaxaca, Mexico. MA thesis, University of North Dakota (xiii+103 pp.). Covers San Martín Duraznos, Guadalupe Nundaca, Santa Catarina Noltepec, Santa Rosa Caxtlahuaca, San Pedro Chayuco, San Miguel Cuevas (all = vmc per Glottolog) plus Yucunicoco.
sources.note: Silent: the word 'stress' does not occur in the body (only in a bibliography title). Ch.3 §3.2 'phonological correspondences' and §3.3 'Tone' are lexicostatistic/tone-pattern comparisons of wordlists; Appendix note (p.~104): underlying CV words are lengthened to CVV or CVʔV 'to satisfy the minimal word constraint of two mora'. downloaded from the the Internet Archive snapshot of the UND Commons PDF (site is could not be reached by automated download).

sources.citation: Duarte Borquez, Claudia. 2023. Tone, prosodic structure and grammatical structure in San Juan Piñas Mixtec (Tò'ōn Ndá'ví). Qualifying paper, UC San Diego.

sources.note: Source of the prosodic-structure analysis (couplet = right-aligned metrical foot) used by Caballero et al. 2026 for a variety whose authors assign it to ISO vmc; a QP on prosodic structure is the likeliest place for an explicit stress/foot-headedness statement. Identity caveat: Glottolog files San Juan Piñas under west2643.
